title: Telemetry-driven action suggester for admin workflows
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Build a suggestion engine that consumes operator telemetry (alerts, SLO breaches, error-trace patterns, console traces) and proposes concrete next steps as pre-populated runbook tasks or automated remedial actions.
Goal: reduce mean time to resolution (MTTR) for common platform incidents by surfacing vetted remediation templates directly in the admin console and in on-call chatflows.

Scope: integrations with metrics/alerting (Prometheus/Alertmanager), tracing/logs (Tempo/Loki), the existing runbooks-as-tasks system, and Slack/Console notification plumbing. Include audit logging and manual approval gates for non-safe actions.
acceptance_criteria: When an alert matching a known pattern fires, the console shows a suggested runbook task created with pre-filled fields (summary, affected services, recommended command/playbook link) with a single-click create action.
Operators can accept, modify, or reject suggestions; accepted suggestions create a tracked runbook task with links to telemetry and an audit trail.
Automated action mode (opt-in per-team) performs low-risk fixes (cache flush, restart staging queue) with configurable safety/approval and logs the change in the runbook task.
False-suggestion rate is tracked and must be below 20% during the initial pilot window, with dashboards available in Console.
All suggested actions and automated executions are recorded in audit logs and appear in the customer workspace for Dedicated/Private deployments per RBAC controls.
design_notes: We will implement a lightweight classifier that maps alert signatures and top-n trace fingerprints to a canonical remediation template ID. Start with rule-based mapping for high-precision patterns, then add a small ML model for fuzzy matching (Phase 2).
Trade-offs: rule-based mapping yields higher precision initially and is easier to audit; ML improves recall but requires labeled incident history and monitoring for drift.

Security: non-destructive actions allowed by default. Any action that touches secrets, modifies KMS keys, or performs tenant-affecting migrations requires explicit approval from an operator with 'admin' role. Design docs linked below.

UX: suggestions surface in three places: (1) Console incident flyout, (2) Slack incident channel thread (via Opsbot), (3) on-call mobile push. Suggestion UI includes confidence score, why-we-suggest (trace snippets/metric cutouts), and links to the runbook step.
implementation_plan: - Data: instrument 30 common alerts and link to canonical remediation templates stored in the runbook registry.
- API: add /suggest endpoint in ops-service that accepts alert payloads and returns suggestion objects (template_id, confidence, required_approval).
- UI: console flyout that shows suggestions and allows one-click task creation. Add Slack message actions via Opsbot integration.
- Safety: approval gating, dry-run mode, audit logging in event-store with immutable IDs.
- Add telemetry similarity matcher and simple gradient-boosted classifier trained on historical incidents.
- Implement per-team opt-in automated action policies and quota controls to limit blast radius.
- Expand pattern coverage, integrate with Dedicated/Private RBAC, add canary rollout for automated actions, and export dashboards for false-positive monitoring.
